question.body:
The function $f$ has derivatives of all orders. Suppose $f(2)=-3$, $f'(2)=5$, $f''(2)=3$, and $f'''(2)=-8$.

(a) Write the third-degree Taylor polynomial for $f$ about $x=2$, then use it to approximate $f(1.5)$.

(b) If $abs(f^(4)(x)) <= 3$ for $1.5 <= x <= 2$, use the Lagrange error bound to explain why $f(1.5) != -5$.

(c) Write the fourth-degree Taylor polynomial $P$ for $g(x)=f(x^2+2)$ about $x=0$. Use $P$ to explain why $g$ has a relative minimum at $x=0$.
question.solution:
(a)
$T_3(x)=-3+5(x-2)+3/2(x-2)^2-4/3(x-2)^3$.
Thus $f(1.5) approx T_3(1.5)=-4.958̅$.

(b) The error is at most
$3/(4!) abs(1.5-2)^4 = 0.0078125$.
Therefore $f(1.5)>-4.958̅-0.0078125>-5$, so $f(1.5) != -5$.

(c) Substituting $x^2+2$ into the needed terms gives
$P(x)=-3+5x^2+3/2x^4$.
The coefficient of $x$ is $0$, so $g'(0)=0$; the coefficient of $x^2$ is $5=g''(0)/2$, so $g''(0)=10>0$. Hence $g$ has a relative minimum at $x=0$.
